column1: # Module 06 — repo archaeology. Format: Text<TAB>Extra<TAB>tags (Extra optional). Card law: anki/CARD-RULES.md
What are the six repo-archaeology passes, in order? {{c1::Signs}} · {{c1::map}} · {{c1::doors}} · {{c1::one vertical slice}} · {{c1::crown jewels}} · {{c1::verdict}}.
column2: Signs = README/claims · doors = entry points · verdict = tests + audit.

column1: Why trace ONE vertical slice instead of skimming folders? {{c1::One true end-to-end trace teaches the architecture}}.
column2: Ten skimmed folders teach nothing testable.

column1: What is an entry point in a codebase? {{c1::Where execution starts}}.
column2: Mains, route roots, service starts, scheduled tasks — most repos have more than you expect.

column1: In psoc-portal, what does every request hit first? {{c1::app/src/proxy.ts — the middleware auth gate}}.
column2: 31 lines of Next.js middleware, before any route.

column1: What is a server action (Next.js), and its trust rule? {{c1::A function forms call that runs on the server}}; it {{c1::re-checks auth because the browser is never trusted}}.
What is a database migration? {{c1::A numbered SQL file changing the DB's shape}}.
column2: The sequence is the schema's version history — psoc has 45.

column1: What is a server component vs a client component? {{c1::Runs on the server, ships HTML}} vs {{c1::runs in the browser, handles interaction}}.
What is a Windows service? {{c1::A background program the OS runs from boot, no window, as a system account}}.
Why is monk-mode's watchdog a separate program? {{c1::A killed process can't resurrect itself}}.
column2: Recovery must live OUTSIDE the thing being killed.

column1: What is monk-mode's 10-second tick, in order? {{c1::Read config}} → {{c1::verify HMAC}} → {{c1::classify heartbeat}} → {{c1::Hold/Lift}} → {{c1::re-apply hosts block + app kills}}.
What does fail-closed mean? {{c1::On any doubt or verification failure, choose the SAFE state}}.
column2: monk-mode keeps blocking; a fire door that fails locked.

column1: What is the atomic-write pattern (AtomicHosts)? {{c1::Write a temp file completely, then swap it in}}.
column2: No half-written file can ever exist.

column1: Why is monk-mode's weak cipher acceptable? {{c1::The threat is tampering, not secrecy — the HMAC stamp does the real work}}.
column2: Edit anything, the stamp breaks, the block holds.

column1: What is an HMAC, in one sentence? {{c1::A keyed signature over data — without the key you can't forge a valid stamp}}.
Why does monk-mode store the partner code as a PBKDF2 hash? {{c1::Verifiable but not recoverable}}.
column2: Salted, deliberately-slow, one-way — the file never contains anything reversible.

column1: What did the TODO greps across psoc and monk-mode teach? {{c1::Read grep results before believing them}}.
column2: psoc's 0 was real discipline; monk-mode's 13 were placeholder-text false positives.

column1: How does every archaeology dig end? {{c1::Explaining one REAL audit finding in your own code}}.
